fix: support simultaneous stdio+http transports via per-transport McpServer instances

The MCP SDK only allows a single transport per Protocol instance, so
running --transport stdio,http crashed with 'Already connected to a
transport'. Replace the single McpServer with a createMcpServer() factory
that creates a fresh instance (with tools registered) for each transport.
Shared infrastructure (bus, context, WebSocket) remains common to all.

fix: create per-request HTTP transport to prevent stateless reuse error

The WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport in stateless mode (no
sessionIdGenerator) is single-use — the SDK throws 'Stateless transport
cannot be reused across requests' on the second call.  Create a fresh
transport and McpServer per HTTP request, matching the official SDK
pattern for stateless Hono servers.

Add disposeMcpServer helper to remove per-request servers from the
tracking set so they can be garbage collected.  Add HTTP transport
tests covering single requests, sequential requests, and cleanup.

fix: register export-diagram handler and support async tool results

causing requests to hang indefinitely. Both bus.ts and main_world-plugin.ts

the Promise object instead of awaiting the resolved value.

refactor(plugin): extract bootstrap to fix extension/plugin drift

Three Draw.io entrypoints (`plugin.ts`, `main_world-plugin.ts`,
`main_world.ts`) had each grown their own copy of the in-page
runtime. The two extension entrypoints were stale forks and
silently lost capabilities the bundled plugin had gained:
document-state listeners (target_document routing), shape
extraction (vendor sidebar shapes), and post-tool syncDocumentState.

Move all three concerns into a single `bootstrapPlugin` in
drawio-mcp-plugin, parameterised by an injected Transport.
Each entrypoint now only owns its host-specific glue:

- plugin.ts / main_world-plugin.ts: WebSocketManager + settings dialog
- main_world.ts: CustomEvent bus to the content script

The content/background relay forwards every WS payload unchanged,
so the regular extension now gets parity with the bundled plugin
(target_document routing and shape extraction work for the first time).

Net -138 lines; `bus.ts` and the four bus-related types in
extension/types.ts are unused after this and removed.

fix(register-tool): strip $schema at tools/list response time

The existing setTimeout-based stripper in createServerWithSchemaStripping
is a no-op against the current MCP SDK (1.29.0 with Zod 4). The SDK now
stores Zod schemas verbatim at registration time in
`_registeredTools[name].inputSchema` and lazily serializes them to JSON
Schema via `z4mini.toJSONSchema` only when a client issues `tools/list`.
The `$schema` key is injected at serialization, not registration — so
the setTimeout that mutates the stored Zod object never sees it.

Net effect: Claude Code sees the `$schema` key on the wire, fails its
own parameter-name validation regex (`^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,64}$`), and
drops the entire `properties` object. The tool name remains exposed
but the LLM has no schema to drive arguments from — tools/call then
fails server-side with "Invalid input: expected object, received string"
because the client sent strings where the server expects objects.

Reproducer (before this patch, against a running server):

  $ curl -s ${MCP_URL} -X POST \
      -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
      -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize",...}' > /dev/null
  $ curl -s ${MCP_URL} -X POST ... -d '{"...","method":"tools/list"}' \
      | jq '.result.tools[] | select(.name=="add-rectangle").inputSchema'

  Returns the full schema but with a leading
    "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"
  which Claude Code's MCP layer then sanitizes by wiping `properties`.

Fix: intercept the inner `Server._requestHandlers` entry for
`"tools/list"` after the SDK has registered it (lazily, on first
`server.tool(...)` call). The wrapper delegates to the original handler
and post-processes each tool's `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` through
the existing `stripSchemaRecursively`.

Verified:
- Local server: $schema is gone, all 9 add-rectangle properties present,
  required: ["target_page"] preserved.
- All 309 unit/integration tests still pass (`pnpm --filter
  drawio-mcp-server run test`).
- No public API change; same `createServerWithSchemaStripping(server)`
  signature, same call site in src/index.ts.

fix(server): release port 3333 on process exit (#60)

Register SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP handlers and stdio stdin EOF
handlers that invoke app.close() before process.exit(0). MCP
hosts (notably Claude Desktop on Windows) signal disconnect by
closing the stdio pipe rather than sending a POSIX signal, so
without a stdin 'end'/'close' listener the WebSocket server kept
the event loop alive and leaked port 3333 across host restarts.

Add stdio-shutdown.test.ts covering SIGTERM, SIGINT, stdio pipe
close, and HTTP-transport SIGTERM. Each asserts process exit and
port release within 5s.

Bump version to 2.1.2.

fix(routing): route drawio tool calls per document.id across tabs

Multiple drawio tabs share one background WebSocket. Previously the
server's ConnectionEntry.document held a single doc, so each tab's
document-state overwrote the previous. list-documents returned only
the last writer. Tool requests were then broadcast to every content
port; the tab whose active id didn't match threw "Target document ...
is no longer active" while the other tab silently ran the tool on the
wrong document.

- Server: ConnectionEntry.documents becomes Map<docId, DocumentInfo>.
  document-state sets by id; new document-removed control removes one.
  list_known_documents/find_connection_by_document_id updated.
- Background: track docId <-> port from observed outbound document-state.
  Route inbound WS payloads carrying target_document.id to the owning
  port only; broadcast remains the fallback for control messages.
  Emit document-removed to server on port disconnect.
- Content: outbound switched from runtime.sendMessage to port.postMessage
  so background can identify the sender frame without extra plumbing.

- Debug-log each shutdown phase for future diagnosis

fix(plugin): sync ui.currentPage state after import-diagram replace (#56)

editor.setGraphXml swaps graph.model.root wholesale but leaves
ui.currentPage.{root,viewState,graphModelNode} pointing at the
pre-import state. Drawio's Page abstraction re-hydrates from those
stale references on the next internal sync (pan, zoom, page-round
trip, save), blanking the canvas and risking a stale serialization
on File > Save even though the live model contains the imported
cells.

Call the existing sync_live_current_page_state helper after both
the replace and new-page branches finish reloading the graph. This
brings page.root back in line with model.root, invalidates the
graphModelNode cache, and refreshes viewState so drawio's next tick
sees consistent state.

Add a real-environment regression test that:
- imports a diagram via replace mode,
- asserts ui.currentPage.root === graph.model.root and
  graphModelNode is null,
- round-trips through a scratch page and confirms the imported cell
  survives.
